statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 venues remain inside the CME weekend halt, with Tail at its structural floor and Stress high.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. CME equity futures are halted until Sunday 22:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop at any point in this horizon. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 carries a record 30,807.93 close through the weekend halt: a completed Friday retracement and a 15.31 VIX keep Tail low, while a 5.28% 10-year, Brent near $102 and a sixth Hormuz tanker strike keep Stress high
body: Friday 2 October closed the Nasdaq-100 at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, but the close sat 209.60 points below the 31,017.53 session high and only 70.86 above the 30,737.07 low. The session therefore ended with its retracement completed rather than holding an extreme, and that distinction carries more weight for this contract than the record itself: extreme-holding is a Tail amplifier, a completed give-back is not. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31 and settled at the bottom of its 15.30-16.24 range, so realised volatility decayed into the close. September payrolls arrived at 29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, with the unemployment rate up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings at +0.1% month-over-month and +3.0% year-over-year. Bond traders cut the implied probability of an October hike to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier, and the broader tape confirmed the risk-positive reading: the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19% to 27,190.86, the S&P 500 added 0.73% to 7,722.72 and the Dow gained 0.49% to 51,176.96. Megacap leadership stayed concentrated, with Nvidia printing an intraday record 237.87 dollars per share at roughly 5.72 trillion dollars of market value and Tesla up about 4% on third-quarter deliveries of 486,532 units. Two carried pressures keep Stress in the high band. The long end did not follow the dovish payrolls print: the 10-year finished at 5.28%, up 0.04 on the day, after trading in its highest region since 2002 earlier in the week, with the 30-year near 5.63%. Energy remains dislocated: the Strait of Hormuz is closed for a 216th day, with a single transit recorded on 27 September against a baseline near 85 per day, and the Kuwait-flagged VLCC Kazimah III and a Panama-flagged tanker were reported struck on 1 and 2 October, the fifth and sixth such strikes since 28 September. Brent is carried near $102.25 while WTI finished at $91.11, down 1.90%, recovering from an $88.06 low after the G7 committed to releasing 100 million barrels of reserves over four months. The decisive structural fact for this horizon is that CME equity futures entered their weekend halt at Friday 21:00Z and do not reopen until Sunday 22:00Z, which is beyond the end of this 24-hour window. No Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any slot published here, so none of the amplifiers this contract requires for elevated Tail, persistent directional efficiency, shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension or sustained extreme-holding, is structurally available. Tail is therefore held at its halt floor and nudged only marginally in the back half to reflect unpriced escalation and energy headlines accumulating behind a closed market. The shared Finviz context file was read and rejected as evidence: its collection timestamp is 29 September and its status is partial, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is far outside the 90-minute freshness contract and is not used to support any conclusion here.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Friday's U.S. session and the first eight hours of the weekend halt. Published Claude history shows Tail peaking in an orange 25-27 band across the 13:00-14:00Z cash-open hours, easing to a yellow 20-24 through the afternoon, then falling into green single digits from 21:00Z as the cash close completed its retracement and CME futures entered the halt. Stress held in a high 71-79 band through the session on the energy and long-end backdrop before easing toward 65, and Confidence ranged between 82 and 89. These are the model's own published opinions at the time and are not restated with hindsight.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which began Friday at 21:00Z and runs until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop and the mapped state is green throughout. Tail holds flat at 8 through the Saturday slots and steps to 9 from 19:00Z purely on unpriced weekend headline risk accumulating behind a closed market, not on any observed structure. Stress eases from 65 to about 63 through the dead Saturday hours, then firms to 68 by the end of the window as a 5.28% 10-year, Brent near $102, a strait closed for a 216th day and the pending G7 reserve-release detail are all carried forward unpriced. Confidence decays from 85 to 74 purely as Friday's verified evidence ages with no live NQ reference to refresh it. The dominant mode shifts from normal to mixed for the Sunday slots to reflect genuinely two-sided unpriced risk rather than observed conflict. Both genuine checkpoints lie beyond this window: Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z on 5 October and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z on 7 October. Any weekend escalation or G7 implementation news could only be priced at the reopen, which is also outside this horizon.
